newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to up limit on advance receipts by exporters.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to up limit on advance receipts by exporters.

text.p: South Korea's Finance and Economy Ministry said on Wednesday it would allow exporters to receive up to 20 percent of their previous year's export amount in advance deposits from October 21, compared with 15 percent at present.
A ministry official said the measure was expected to help ease fund shortages at export companies. These firms are currently suffering under slowing exports and falling export prices.
The ministry would also lengthen the payment period for deferred-payment raw material imports to help competitiveness of local manufacturers, the official said.
Large firms could now import crude oil used in the manufacturing of export items on a deferred-payment contract for up to 180 days, against 150 days at present, a ministry statement said.

The maximum deferred-payment period for smaller firms' raw material imports from "nearby regions" -- Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong and the Philippines -- for use in manufacturing export items would be raised to 150 days from 120 days at present.
